title: Verifier identity & lifecycle
canonical_definition: Register, activate, suspend, rotate and retire verifier identities without granting unrelated authority.

milestone_relationship.rationale: This is the first runtime slice of CMP-1.4. Broader app-specific integration is deferred until verifier identity, classes/capabilities and verification-policy registry converge.

implementation.rotation: Governance proposes; the new authority must accept; accepted rotation lands SUSPENDED and requires fresh activation.
implementation.identity: Domain-separated chain/contract/serial verifier ID with exact revision history and current authority reverse lookup.

authority_boundaries: Registration establishes verifier identity only and does not grant verification capability.

Identity/lifecycle does not assign verifier class, workload capability, profile, appointment, independence, correctness, settlement, custody, stake/slash, governance, worker, validator, bridge or arbitrary-wallet authority.
Activation is an administrative lifecycle gate, not proof of correctness or independence.
Suspension blocks current identity eligibility but does not rewrite historical revisions or verdict evidence.
Retirement is terminal for the verifier identity.
Rotation cannot silently redirect an active verifier identity: governance proposes, the new authority accepts, and reactivation is explicit.
exit_criteria: Verifier identities can be registered with domain-separated IDs and immutable revision history.
Only governance can activate and retire verifier identities.
Active verifier authorities can fail-closed suspend themselves; governance can suspend them.
Rotation requires governance proposal plus acceptance by the new authority and cannot auto-reactivate.
Retired identities cannot be reactivated or rotated.
Exact-current identity eligibility fails closed for stale revisions, wrong authorities and non-ACTIVE status.
No unrelated authority is granted by registration or lifecycle state.
